topics.label: Lecture introduction and scope
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity detects infection and damage through molecular patterns and appropriately positioned, germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptors and their signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate recognition at different cellular locations into appropriate inflammatory or antiviral responses.

topics.label: Other pattern recognition receptors and the inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics extend recognition beyond toll-like receptors to show how additional danger-sensing mechanisms activate inflammation and contribute to inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel cells initiate local and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how activated sentinel cells convert danger recognition into inflammatory signals whose reach depends on their abundance.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment to inflamed tissue
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic follows the mechanism that brings circulating leukocytes out of blood vessels and guides them to an infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how lymphatic drainage enables activated dendritic cells to carry evidence of infection to lymph nodes for adaptive immune activation.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory responses that are useful locally become dangerous when excessive activation produces systemic cardiovascular effects.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through a changing balance between inflammatory stimulation and mechanisms that suppress it.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why recovery after inflammation may fail to restore normal tissue, with persistent inflammation sometimes serving to contain an otherwise unresolved threat.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces complement as the subject of the next lecture.
